clue.text: Pop singers reformed, giving up gin fizz for crush

indicators.note: the remaining letters of the singers are formed again into a new order
giving something up means letting it go, so these letters are taken away

parts.note: the gin is fizzed, stirred up, so its letters come out as I, N, G in that order

explanation.surface: A pop group splits up and the members swap their gin fizzes for a fruit crush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin fizz' stirs GIN into ING, which 'giving up' takes out of POPSINGERS to leave POPSERS; 'reformed' rearranges those into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To crush people is to subdue them harshly, the same as to tyrannise or persecute them.

clue.text: Standard tuner ignores second and better half

parts.note: par is the standard or norm, as in golf

indicators.note: the second letter of the word tuner is left out

explanation.surface: A piano tuner of the usual sort pays no attention to the timekeeping or to his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ignores second' drops U, the second letter of TUNER, leaving TNER.
explanation.definitionFit: Better half is a jokey idiom for a spouse, someone's life companion.

clue.text: Cuts short recapitulations, except for cello's opening

indicators.note: everything is kept apart from the named letter, which is removed

parts.note: recaps is the shortened form of recapitulations

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A performer trims the reprises of a piece, leaving only the cellist's opening passage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'except for' removes C, the opening of 'cello's', from RECAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: To reap is to cut a crop at harvest, so reaps means cuts.

clue.text: Complications in section of 14

explanation.definitionFit: Strings attached are hidden conditions, and the violins, violas, cellos and basses form the strings section.

clue.text: Computer baron attends the controversial Verdi opera

parts.note: a Mac is an Apple computer

indicators.note: something controversial stirs things up, so these letters are disturbed

explanation.surface: A tech tycoon goes to a contentious production of a Verdi opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 'controversial' rearranges THE into ETH; 'attends' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Macbeth is Verdi's opera based on Shakespeare's Scottish play.

clue.text: Sharp bass impressed Queen's 2

definitions.note: entry 2 is PARTNER, so this means the Queen's consort

indicators.note: pressed into, so one piece is set inside the other

parts.note: sharp means quick-witted, alert
B is the abbreviation for bass in music

explanation.surface: A keen bass singer made an impression on the Queen's husband.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Victoria's husband was Prince Albert; entry 2 is PARTNER, so 'Queen's 2' means her consort.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Albert was Queen Victoria's husband and consort.

clue.text: Britten opera poster put up by posh churchman

parts.note: a bill is a poster stuck up on a wall

indicators.note: in a down clue, putting something up means writing it upwards, backwards

parts.note: U means upper-class, posh
DD is a Doctor of Divinity, a churchman

explanation.surface: A notice advertising a Britten opera has been pinned up by a grand clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' reverses BY to YB. U is upper-class in British usage; DD stands for Doctor of Divinity.
explanation.definitionFit: Billy Budd is Benjamin Britten's opera after Melville's naval story.

clue.text: Measure songster's tempo?

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird, a songster
rate means speed or tempo

explanation.surface: A question about how fast a songbird sings.
explanation.definitionFit: To titrate is to measure the concentration of a solution by adding a reagent.

clue.text: RADA duos stumbled into old Peruvian dancer

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Incan describes the old Inca people of Peru

indicators.note: stumbling means falling over awkwardly, so these letters fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Two drama-school pairs trip and fall into an ancient Peruvian dancer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stumbled' rearranges the drama-school letters into SADORADU, set by 'into' inside the Peruvian word. RADA is London's Royal Academy of Dramatic Art.
explanation.definitionFit: Isadora Duncan was the pioneering American modern dancer of the early twentieth century.

clue.text: Leading girl in musical doesn't start solo

indicators.note: the first letter is dropped

parts.note: Maria is the heroine of West Side Story and The Sound of Music

explanation.surface: A musical's heroine fails to come in on her solo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't start' drops M from MARIA.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is an operatic piece for one voice, a solo song.

clue.text: Laughter tracks swamp Iago's intro in Tbilisi complex

indicators.note: to swamp is to engulf, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: RY is short for railway, a set of tracks

indicators.note: the intro to a word is its first letter
complex means tangled, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Canned laughter drowns out the opening of Iago in a Georgian theatre complex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' mixes Iago's intro with the city name to make ISIBILIT, which 'swamp' wraps in the railway abbreviation; Tbilisi is the capital of Georgia.
explanation.definitionFit: Risibility is the tendency to laugh, or the laughter something provokes.

clue.text: Succeeded in match played at the same pitch

definitions.note: adverbial phrase for the noun, as in 'in unison'

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a match is a union, a marriage
S is an abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A successful marriage whose partners sang in perfect harmony.
explanation.definitionFit: Unison is music sung or played with all parts sounding one identical note.

clue.text: A Byrd composition in governor's race meeting

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: a dey was an Ottoman governor of Algiers

indicators.note: composing arranges things, so these letters are put together afresh

explanation.surface: A piece by the composer Byrd is performed at the governor's horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composition' rearranges the composer's name with A into RBYDA, placed by 'in' within the governor. Derby Day is the day of the Epsom Derby horse race.
explanation.definitionFit: Derby Day is the day of the famous Epsom horse race meeting.

clue.text: She's nervous in court among odd Scottish players

indicators.note: set amid, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: orra is a Scots word for odd or spare

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other
being nervous is being jittery, so these letters are shaken up

parts.note: the pronoun she, with the 's as a linking is

explanation.surface: A jittery woman in court sits among peculiar Scots musicians.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nervous' reworks the pronoun as HES, which 'in' sets inside the court abbreviation; 'among' then puts that within the Scots word.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a large ensemble of instrumental players.

clue.text: Hotel hosts old and new boring music

parts.note: H is Hotel in the radio alphabet

indicators.note: boring into something goes into it, so these letters sit inside

parts.note: a host is an army, so hosts are armies

explanation.surface: A hotel lays on music, both traditional and modern, that bores the guests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hosts' looks like the hotel's verb but it is a noun meaning armies. 'boring' puts O and N into ARMIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmonies are combinations of notes sounding together, a kind of music.

clue.text: Britten's friend valued being regularly selected

indicators.note: every other letter is chosen at regular intervals

explanation.surface: A close friend of the composer was prized and often chosen.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking alternate letters across the two words gives A, U, D, E and N.
explanation.definitionFit: W. H. Auden was the poet who collaborated with and befriended Benjamin Britten.

clue.text: 20 film music in a lot of bars

definitions.meaning: twenty items make one of these

definitions.text: film music in a lot of bars
definitions.meaning: a soundtrack written out across many bars of music

explanation.definitionFit: A score is twenty, and also the written music for a film, set out in bars.

clue.text: Smaller version of 14's wee container

definitions.meaning: a ... orchestra is a small version of entry 14

explanation.definitionFit: A chamber orchestra is a small-scale ensemble; a chamber pot is a bedroom vessel for urine.

clue.text: Delius' debut in E minor in a broadcast of the early 20th century

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the letter E from the key name
a ward is a minor under a guardian's care

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so the first letter
broadcasting scatters things widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A Delius piece in E minor is broadcast as a period work from the 1900s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'E minor' looks like a musical key but splits into a letter and a ward; 'in' slips Delius' first letter between them, and 'broadcast' rearranges the second 'in a' into IAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edwardian era is the reign of Edward VII, 1901 to 1910.

clue.text: Songs of Praise hasn't managed to retain big space

indicators.note: retaining something means holding it inside
managed means handled or arranged, so these letters are reorganised

parts.note: an em is a wide printing space

explanation.surface: The hymn-singing TV programme has failed to keep a large venue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'managed' rearranges the contraction into ANTHS and 'to retain' holds the printers' space inside. Songs of Praise is a long-running BBC television hymn programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Anthems are choral songs praising God or a nation.

clue.text: Hinted Jones the singer's bordering on loud nonetheless

indicators.note: one piece borders another on both sides, enclosing it

parts.note: Aled Jones is a Welsh singer

indicators.note: read as none less, so a zero, the letter O, is taken away from the word loud

explanation.surface: Hinted that the Welsh singer was close to being loud anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonetheless' is read as 'none less', taking a zero out of the volume word; 'bordering on' then has the singer's name enclose the rest. Aled Jones is a Welsh singer and broadcaster.
explanation.definitionFit: To allude is to refer indirectly, so alluded means hinted.

clue.text: 28 quality needs vocalic change for hymn

indicators.note: one vowel is swapped for another

parts.note: entry 28 is IRKSOME, and tedium is the quality of being irksome

explanation.surface: A dull, plodding character needs a change of vowel to make a hymn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs vocalic change' swaps the I of TEDIUM for E.
explanation.definitionFit: The Te Deum is an ancient Latin hymn of praise to God.

clue.text: Christmas opus, a new revolutionary early 19th-century piece

indicators.note: revolving turns things round, so the whole run reads backwards

parts.note: Noel means Christmas

explanation.surface: A Christmas composition becomes a fresh revolutionary piece from the 1800s.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' reverses NOELOPAN. The napoleon was a French gold twenty-franc coin; 'revolutionary' also hints at the man.
explanation.definitionFit: A napoleon was a French gold coin, a piece minted under the emperor in the early 1800s.

clue.text: Son chops lutes in bits for scrap

indicators.note: chopping cuts into something, so one piece goes in
broken in bits, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: A boy smashes lutes to pieces for scrap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in bits' rearranges LUTES to TUSLE, which S 'chops' into.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is a scuffle or fight, the same as a tussle.

clue.text: Pears played extra version of 3

indicators.note: the letters are played around with into a new order

explanation.surface: Peter Pears sang an additional version of a piece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'version of 3' adds a second hint: the answer is also a rearrangement of entry 3. Peter Pears was a tenor and Britten's partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Spare means additional or surplus, the same as extra.

clue.text: Erase a libretto rewritten by egghead

indicators.note: rewriting arranges the letters afresh

parts.note: the head of egg is its first letter, E

explanation.surface: An intellectual wipes out a libretto and rewrites it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewritten' turns A LIBRETTO into OBLITERAT; E is the head of 'egg'.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate is to wipe out entirely, to erase.

clue.text: Perfect haircut for Verdi opera

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, perfect, written as AI
DA is the duck's arse, a 1950s haircut

explanation.surface: A singer asks for a perfect hairdo for the Verdi opera.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 is written with I for the figure 1. The DA is a slicked-back 1950s hairstyle.
explanation.definitionFit: Aida is Verdi's opera about an Ethiopian princess in Egypt.

clue.text: No ornate coda in revised Mikado score? That's annoying

indicators.note: revising changes the order, so the remainder is rearranged
no means without, so these letters are removed

parts.note: an ornate coda is an elaborated one, its letters rearranged as A, D, O, C

explanation.surface: Revising Gilbert and Sullivan's score without its showy ending would be a nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ornate' rearranges CODA to ADOC, removed from MIKADOSCORE ('No'); 'revised' rearranges the remaining MIKSORE.
explanation.definitionFit: Irksome describes something tiresome or irritating.

clue.text: What lark does musically when cycle finishes?

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
c is the abbreviation for cycle, as in cycles per second
ends means finishes

explanation.surface: A question about the lark's song at the close of a song cycle.
explanation.walkthrough: Vaughan Williams's piece The Lark Ascending supplies the musical definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark rises as it sings, and the famous music describes it ascending.
